title: Onko with singular owners
focus: Add the yes/no question ending -ko to on: on + -ko = onko. Use onko with every owner, including meillä, teillä, and heillä.

exercises.prompt: Choose “Does he have a pen?” in Finnish. Use hänellä (“he as the owner”) and kynä (“a pen”). Frame: “___ hänellä kynä”.
exercises.explanation: On + the yes/no question ending -ko gives onko. Put onko first and keep it fixed for every owner.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed onko in possession questions: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.Onko hänellä kynä?: On + the yes/no question ending -ko gives onko. Put onko first and keep it fixed for every owner.
optionFeedback.Ovatko hänellä kynä?: On + the yes/no question ending -ko gives onko. Put onko first and keep it fixed for every owner. This choice uses the wrong verb form.
This choice changes the required polarity or leaves the required question pattern.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: onko + possessor + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.formation: On + the yes/no question ending -ko = onko. It stays the same with every possessor.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: hän has the learned possession form hänellä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
kynä stays in its basic singular form: one pen.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed onko in possession questions: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
